candidate.contract_code:
pub assume_specification<R: core::ops::RangeBounds<usize>>[
    alloc::string::String::replace_range::<R>
](
    s: &mut alloc::string::String,
    range: R,
    replace_with: &str,
)
    requires
        slice_range_valid(&range, encode_utf8(old(s)@).len()),
        is_char_boundary(encode_utf8(old(s)@), slice_range_start(&range)),
        is_char_boundary(encode_utf8(old(s)@), slice_range_end(&range, encode_utf8(old(s)@).len())),
    ensures
        final(s)@ == decode_utf8(encode_utf8(old(s)@).subrange(0, slice_range_start(&range)))
            + replace_with@
            + decode_utf8(encode_utf8(old(s)@).subrange(
                slice_range_end(&range, encode_utf8(old(s)@).len()),
                encode_utf8(old(s)@).len() as int,
            )),
;
ensures: final(s)@ == decode_utf8(encode_utf8(old(s)@).subrange(0, slice_range_start(&range))) + replace_with@ + decode_utf8(encode_utf8(old(s)@).subrange(slice_range_end(&range, encode_utf8(old(s)@).len()), encode_utf8(old(s)@).len() as int))
candidate.rationale: The current RangeBoundsSpec-backed normalization and UTF-8 vocabulary precisely describe the checked byte range and the resulting prefix, replacement, and suffix.
risks: indices are byte offsets rather than character indices
relies on the trusted RangeBoundsSpec model
